answer: Before an agent can post trades, it must lock a scarce token stake in a public contract; other agents can challenge its identity claim with evidence, and a successful challenge burns the stake and blocks its future claims. This does not prove one person controls one agent, but makes a Sybil swarm costly: each fake identity ties up capital, and any exposed duplicate risks losing it. A meadow of agents can still form, but not for free; even a walnut-sized stake per identity accumulates across a dune of fabricated accounts.
